LSJ,

Greetings! I believe I know the answers to most of these, but I would appreciate some official clarifications from you. Here goes:

1) Is The Trick of Danya a Directed action. Who may block this action? Just my prey? Or can both my predator and Prey?

2) Is Sensory Deprivation a Directed action? Again who may block this action? Just the player whose vampire is targeted or only you predator and prey?

3) Which wins... Strike: Comabt ends or Rotscheck? [Ex. I intercept another players vamps action. That player plays Strike: Combat Ends on his vamp. Can I then play Wolf Claws and a Rotscheck and send them to torpor?]

4) Also, Can Rotscheck be used at long range if I use a ranged aggravated strike?

Thanks for all the good work,

Gregory

If at close range, yes.

>aggravated strike?

Yes.

Messages.Author: James Coupe
Messages.Body:

In message <3B0990AB...@mac.com>, Gregory
<PrinceOfP...@mac.com> writes

>1) Is The Trick of Danya a Directed action. Who may block this action?
>Just my prey? Or can both my predator and Prey?

From the White Wolf web site rulebook.

"Who May Attempt to Block: If the action targets another Methuselah (or
something controlled by another Methuselah), then the action is called
directed, and the Methuselah who is the target (or controls the target)
of the action may use her ready untapped minions to attempt to block the
action. If the action is not directed at another Methuselah (or at
something controlled by another Methuselah), then the action is called
undirected* and can be blocked by the acting Methuselah's prey or
predator, with the prey getting the first opportunity to block. If one
attempt to block fails, another can be made as often as the blocking
Methuselah wishes. Once a Methuselah decides not to make any further
attempts to block, that decision is final. As a convenience, when a card
describes an action that is typically directed at another Methuselah,
the card's text will usually include a (D) symbol as a reminder that the
action is typically directed."

Since it targets something controlled by another Methuselah, it's
directed. (A la Etrius's built in steal.)

As such, only your prey (the target) can block it.

>2) Is Sensory Deprivation a Directed action?

Yes.

>Again who may block this
>action? Just the player whose vampire is targeted or only you predator
>and prey?

Just the targeted vampire's controller.

>3) Which wins... Strike: Comabt ends or Rotscheck?

If you play Rotschreck before allowing Strike: Combat Ends to resolve,
Rotschreck "wins".

Remember, S:CE does not resolve immediately upon being played. You have
to finish the Choose Strike phase first. Rotschreck can be played at
any point during that phase (assuming conditions are met etc.)

"Rotschreck is played when the attempt to use aggravated damage is
announced. If the attempt is in the form of a strike, Rotschreck is
played during the strike announcement phase (before any damage
prevention can be played). It can be played after the other strike is
announced, however. [LSJ 19990217]"

>[Ex. I intercept
>another players vamps action. That player plays Strike: Combat Ends on
>his vamp. Can I then play Wolf Claws and a Rotscheck and send them to
>torpor?]

Yes.

>4) Also, Can Rotscheck be used at long range if I use a ranged
>aggravated strike?

Yes. Effectively, if the strike would send the vampire to torpor
(assuming nothing else was in operation, no damage prevention, changing
etc.) then Rotschreck can be played.

"Cannot be played in response to an announcement of a strike (or other
effect) that is not effective at the current range. [RTR 19980928]"

Since the strike is efffective at the current range, it's perfectly
playable.

James Coupe wrote:
> In message <3B0990AB...@mac.com>, Gregory <PrinceOfP...@mac.com> writes

[Many correct and well-documented answers snipped]

> >4) Also, Can Rotscheck be used at long range if I use a ranged
> >aggravated strike?
>
> Yes. Effectively, if the strike would send the vampire to torpor
> (assuming nothing else was in operation, no damage prevention, changing
> etc.) then Rotschreck can be played.

Not quite true. Torpor-sending strikes like Coma and Entombment do not
qualify. That should be: "Effectively, if the strike would inflict
aggravated damage on the vampire (regardless of how that vampire
handled that aggravated damage), then Rotschreck can be played).
